Title: a Conventional Commit subject of at most 72 characters, such as `feat: add the map editor`. The title is the only part of this pull request that reaches git history.

Breaking change: add `!` after the type in the title, and put a `> [!IMPORTANT]` alert above Why that says what breaks and how to migrate.

Write for a reviewer who has only this pull request. Re-read the body before you open it, since auto-merge leaves no later chance to fix it.
-->

## Why

<!-- The problem and its impact, and why this approach beat the alternatives. Summarize a linked issue instead of only linking it. -->

## Testing

<!-- The manual steps you took and what you observed. Leave out CI output, since the checks show on the pull request. When you did not test the change, write "Not tested" and why. -->

## Notes for reviewers

<!-- Optional: where to start reading, what is risky, and what you are unsure of. Delete this section when you have nothing to add. -->

<!--
End with one line per linked issue, and leave the lines out when no issue applies:

Closes #<number>
Refs: #<number>

Closes links the issue, which moves its project item to In review, and closes it on merge. Never close an Epic. Refs marks an issue this change only touches; it neither links the issue nor moves its item. Write owner/repo#<number> for an issue in another repository.
-->
